findings.evidence: Lines 330–368 and 381–443 expose both bodies while already supplying the observable API, including `conjNormalRep_ρ`, `conjNormalFDRep_ρ`, and `res_conj*`.
findings.fix: Remove both `@[expose]` attributes and prove the characteristic lemmas internally with `:= (rfl)` or explicit unfolding where needed.
findings.issue: `conjNormalRep` and `conjNormalFDRep` (line 381) are marked `@[expose]` despite having `V`, `ρ`, character, dimension, and comparison lemmas; consumers can unnecessarily depend on their `Rep.res`/`Action.res` implementation.

findings.evidence: `rg` finds only `conjNormalRep_one`/`conjNormalRep_mul` and their FDRep mirrors at lines 362–425; the roadmap README line 234 explicitly requires an autoequivalence/action on `Rep k N`.
findings.fix: Bundle `conjNormalRep` and `conjNormalFDRep` as `MulAction`s (and expose the normal-subgroup endofunctor/autoequivalence required by the roadmap), using the one/mul coherence as laws.
findings.issue: The file calls these operations a genuine `G`-action, but only exports object functions and equations; there is no `SMul`/`MulAction` instance, normal conjugation functor, or autoequivalence, so downstream orbit/stabilizer and categorical APIs cannot consume the promised action.

findings.evidence: The corresponding identity laws at lines 361 and 418 are `@[simp]`, while both parallel multiplication laws lack any automation annotation.
findings.fix: Mark both multiplication laws `@[simp]`, or obtain the standard simp-normalized `mul_smul` law from the bundled `MulAction` interface.
findings.issue: `conjNormalRep_mul` and `conjNormalFDRep_mul` (line 423) are unannotated even though they are the action multiplication normal forms and should simplify conjugation by a product.

summary: The normal-subgroup operations expose implementation bodies but do not provide the bundled action/autoequivalence interface promised by the roadmap. Their multiplication laws also lack normal-form automation.
